demoDataNotice: CURATED DEMO CONTENT FOR ACADEMIC DEMONSTRATION. These entries are general, patient-facing summaries written for this project from publicly available patient information leaflets and standard formulary guidance. They are deliberately GENERAL: no entry contains a dose, a treatment decision or advice for an individual. This is not a substitute for the leaflet supplied with your medicine or for advice from your pharmacist or doctor.
sourceNotes: Content is hand-written summary text held in this repository. The assistant retrieves and returns these entries verbatim - it does not generate medical text at answer time, and it cannot answer about a medicine that is not in this file.

mayAnswer: What it is commonly used for
When to contact a doctor or pharmacist
mustRefuse: Diagnosing a condition or explaining what a symptom means for the user
Suggesting, changing, starting or stopping a dose
Advising whether to stop or continue treatment
Answering whether two medicines interact (this is handled by the separate deterministic interaction dataset)
Anything specific to pregnancy, breastfeeding, children or a personal medical condition

commonUses: Relief of mild to moderate pain such as headache, toothache or period pain
Reducing fever
entries.howItWorks: Paracetamol is thought to reduce the production of prostaglandins in the brain, which lowers the perception of pain and helps bring down a fever.
generalPrecautions: Do not exceed the maximum daily amount stated on the pack - for most adults this is 4 g (usually eight 500 mg tablets) in 24 hours.
Paracetamol is present in many combination cold and flu remedies. Check every label so you do not take it twice.
Take extra care if you have liver problems or drink alcohol regularly.
Leave at least 4 hours between doses.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place, in the original pack, away from direct sunlight and out of the reach of children.
commonSideEffects: Side effects are uncommon at normal doses
Rarely: skin rash or an allergic reaction
talkToYourDoctorIf: You have taken more than the daily maximum, even if you feel well - overdose can damage the liver and needs urgent attention.
Your pain or fever lasts more than three days.
You develop a rash, swelling or difficulty breathing.

commonUses: Pain relief, particularly where there is inflammation
Reducing fever
Muscular and joint aches, period pain
entries.howItWorks: Ibuprofen blocks the COX enzymes that produce prostaglandins, chemicals involved in pain, swelling and fever.
generalPrecautions: Take with or just after food to reduce stomach irritation.
Use the lowest dose that works, for the shortest time.
Not suitable for everyone - people with stomach ulcers, asthma, kidney disease, heart failure or who are pregnant should check first.
Avoid taking more than one anti-inflammatory painkiller at the same time.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Keep liquid preparations tightly closed and out of the reach of children.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You get stomach pain, black stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
You have unexplained swelling of the ankles.
You are taking a blood thinner, another anti-inflammatory, or medicines for blood pressure.

commonUses: Low dose: helping to prevent blood clots after a heart attack or stroke
Higher dose: pain and fever relief
entries.howItWorks: Aspirin irreversibly blocks an enzyme in platelets, making them less likely to clump together and form a clot. At higher doses it also reduces pain and inflammation.
generalPrecautions: Low-dose aspirin is usually taken long term - do not stop it without medical advice.
Take with or after food.
Aspirin increases bleeding risk, especially alongside other blood thinners or anti-inflammatory painkillers.
Aspirin should not be given to children under 16 unless a doctor has specifically prescribed it.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Aspirin absorbs moisture and smells of vinegar when it has degraded - discard tablets that smell strongly.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You notice unusual bruising, nosebleeds, blood in urine or black stools.
You need surgery or dental work - mention you take aspirin.
You develop ringing in the ears.

commonUses: Managing type 2 diabetes, usually as the first medicine tried
Sometimes used in polycystic ovary syndrome
entries.howItWorks: Metformin reduces the amount of glucose the liver releases and helps the body respond better to its own insulin. It does not usually cause low blood sugar on its own.
generalPrecautions: Take with or just after food to reduce stomach upset.
Slow-release tablets must be swallowed whole, not crushed or chewed.
Tell your doctor before any scan using a contrast dye, or before surgery.
Stop and seek advice if you become severely dehydrated (prolonged vomiting or diarrhoea).
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, in the original blister pack.
commonSideEffects: Nausea, diarrhoea or a metallic taste, usually settling after a few weeks
talkToYourDoctorIf: You have severe or persistent vomiting or diarrhoea.
You develop unusual muscle pain, deep rapid breathing or extreme tiredness.
Your blood sugar readings are consistently outside the range you were given.

commonUses: Lowering high blood pressure
Preventing chest pain (angina)
entries.howItWorks: Amlodipine relaxes the muscle in blood vessel walls so the vessels widen, which lowers blood pressure and improves blood flow to the heart.
generalPrecautions: Take at about the same time each day.
It may take a few weeks for the full effect on blood pressure.
Do not stop suddenly without advice, even if you feel well - high blood pressure usually has no symptoms.
Grapefruit juice can increase the amount of amlodipine in the blood.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light.
commonSideEffects: Flushing or headache, often improving after the first weeks
Feeling dizzy, especially when standing up quickly
talkToYourDoctorIf: Your ankle swelling becomes troublesome.
You faint or feel very dizzy.
You develop chest pain that is new or worse.

commonUses: Lowering cholesterol
Reducing the risk of heart attack and stroke
entries.howItWorks: Atorvastatin blocks HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol, which lowers LDL cholesterol in the blood.
generalPrecautions: Usually taken once a day; it can be taken at any time of day but keep it consistent.
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice.
Continue any diet and exercise advice alongside the medicine.
Some antibiotics and antifungals interact with statins - always mention your statin when prescribed something new.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place in the original pack.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You get unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, particularly with a fever or dark urine.
You develop yellowing of the skin or eyes.
You become pregnant or are planning to.

commonUses: Reducing stomach acid in reflux, heartburn and indigestion
Treating and preventing stomach ulcers
Protecting the stomach alongside anti-inflammatory painkillers
entries.howItWorks: Omeprazole switches off the acid pumps in the stomach lining, substantially reducing acid production.
generalPrecautions: Usually taken 30-60 minutes before a meal, most often before breakfast.
Capsules should be swallowed whole.
Long-term use is reviewed periodically - ask at your next appointment whether you still need it.
It can affect the absorption of some other medicines; space them apart if advised.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place. Keep the bottle tightly closed - the capsules are sensitive to moisture.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You have difficulty swallowing, keep vomiting, or vomit blood.
You notice black stools or unexplained weight loss.
Symptoms return quickly once the course finishes.

commonUses: Treating an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)
entries.howItWorks: Levothyroxine replaces the thyroxine hormone the thyroid gland is not producing in sufficient amounts.
generalPrecautions: Take on an empty stomach, usually 30-60 minutes before breakfast, with water.
Separate it by at least 4 hours from calcium, iron, antacids and some other supplements, which block its absorption.
Keep to the same brand where possible, and take it at the same time each day.
Dose changes are guided by blood tests - never adjust it yourself.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place, protected from light. Levothyroxine is sensitive to heat and humidity.
commonSideEffects: At the correct dose there should be no side effects
Too high a dose can cause palpitations, tremor, sweating or weight loss
talkToYourDoctorIf: You have palpitations, a persistent tremor or feel unusually hot and anxious.
You become pregnant - the dose often needs review.
You start or stop another medicine, especially calcium, iron or an antacid.

commonUses: Preventing and treating blood clots
Reducing stroke risk in atrial fibrillation
Protecting mechanical heart valves
entries.howItWorks: Warfarin reduces the liver's production of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, making the blood less likely to clot.
generalPrecautions: The dose is set by regular INR blood tests and can change often - always follow the most recent instruction.
Keep your intake of green leafy vegetables (vitamin K) reasonably consistent rather than avoiding them entirely.
Many medicines, including some antibiotics and painkillers, change how warfarin works - check before starting anything new, including over-the-counter products.
Carry your anticoagulant card and mention warfarin before any procedure, including dental work.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place in the original container, out of the reach of children.
commonSideEffects: Minor bleeding, for example from the gums when brushing
talkToYourDoctorIf: You have bleeding that will not stop, blood in urine or stools, or black tarry stools.
You have a fall or hit your head.
You miss doses or are unsure what dose to take.

commonUses: Treating bacterial infections of the chest, ear, throat, sinuses, skin and urinary tract
entries.howItWorks: Amoxicillin stops bacteria building their cell walls, which kills the bacteria.
generalPrecautions: Finish the whole course even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
It has no effect on viral infections such as a common cold or flu.
Tell your doctor if you have ever had a reaction to penicillin.
Space doses evenly through the day.
entries.storage: Store capsules and tablets below 25°C in a dry place. Reconstituted liquid usually needs refrigeration and is discarded after 7 to 14 days - check the label.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You develop a rash, swelling of the face or lips, or difficulty breathing - seek urgent help.
You get severe or watery diarrhoea during or after the course.
Symptoms do not improve after two to three days.

commonUses: Treating chest, throat, ear, skin and some sexually transmitted infections
entries.howItWorks: Azithromycin stops bacteria from producing the proteins they need to multiply.
generalPrecautions: Often a short course of 3 to 5 days; finish it as prescribed.
Can be taken with or without food, though food may reduce stomach upset.
Separate it from antacids containing aluminium or magnesium by 2 hours.
Tell your doctor if you have a heart rhythm problem.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place. Shake liquid preparations well before each dose.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You develop palpitations or fainting.
You get severe watery diarrhoea.
You develop yellowing of the skin or eyes.

commonUses: Relief of hay fever and allergy symptoms
Relief of itching from hives
entries.howItWorks: Cetirizine blocks histamine, the chemical released during an allergic reaction that causes sneezing, itching and a runny nose.
generalPrecautions: Usually once a day.
It causes less drowsiness than older antihistamines, but some people are still affected - see how it affects you before driving.
Alcohol can add to any drowsiness.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
talkToYourDoctorIf: Symptoms persist despite treatment.
You have severe swelling of the face, lips or throat - seek urgent help.

commonUses: Quick relief of asthma symptoms such as wheeze, cough and breathlessness
Relief of breathlessness in some lung conditions
entries.howItWorks: Salbutamol relaxes the muscle around the airways within minutes, opening them up so breathing becomes easier.
generalPrecautions: This is a reliever, not a preventer - it does not treat the underlying inflammation.
Needing it more than three times a week usually means asthma control should be reviewed.
Learn and check your inhaler technique; a spacer helps a great deal.
Always carry it with you and check the expiry and dose counter.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C. Do not puncture or burn the canister, and do not leave it in a hot car or in direct sunlight.
talkToYourDoctorIf: Your inhaler is not helping as much as usual, or you need it more often.
You are breathless at rest or cannot speak in full sentences - this is an emergency.
You wake at night with symptoms.

commonUses: Reducing inflammation in conditions such as asthma flare-ups, arthritis, allergic reactions and inflammatory bowel disease
entries.howItWorks: Prednisolone is a synthetic version of a hormone the body makes naturally; it damps down inflammation and the immune response.
generalPrecautions: Take in the morning with or after food unless told otherwise.
Do not stop a longer course suddenly - the dose is usually reduced gradually.
Carry a steroid card for longer courses, and tell any healthcare professional you are taking it.
Avoid contact with chickenpox, shingles or measles if you have not had them, and seek advice if exposed.
entries.storage: Store below 25°C in a dry place.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You feel very unwell, feverish, or develop signs of infection.
Your blood sugar readings rise sharply.
You have severe stomach pain or black stools.
You have marked mood changes.

commonUses: Reducing stomach acid in reflux and ulcers
Stomach protection alongside medicines that irritate the stomach
entries.howItWorks: Pantoprazole blocks the acid pumps in the stomach lining, reducing acid production.
generalPrecautions: Usually taken before breakfast.
Swallow tablets whole - do not crush or chew.
Often preferred over omeprazole for people taking clopidogrel.
Review long-term use periodically.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place in the original pack.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You vomit blood or notice black stools.
You have difficulty swallowing or unexplained weight loss.

commonUses: Lowering high blood pressure
Protecting the kidneys in diabetes
Reducing strain on the heart
entries.howItWorks: Losartan blocks the action of angiotensin II, a hormone that narrows blood vessels, so the vessels relax and blood pressure falls.
generalPrecautions: Take at the same time each day.
You may feel dizzy on the first few doses, particularly when standing up.
Kidney function and potassium are usually checked with blood tests.
Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless advised.
Not suitable in pregnancy.
entries.storage: Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from moisture.
talkToYourDoctorIf: You become pregnant.
You have severe dizziness or faint.
You develop swelling of the face, lips or tongue - seek urgent help.
